item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Alright, thanks for the feedback everyone.

So, yes, it is a pretty simple reference gag. If that doesn't do it for you, I understand. I do think it's more than just containment breaches and combat scenes, though. I wanted to leave the text broad enough to include things like junior researchers avoiding their boss while goofing off, or people going out of their way to duck unwanted conversations.

I've also removed the 682 reference, as I understand why that irks people. I replaced it with 106, because it's difficult to think of a relatively straight-forward dangerous escape-prone SCP outside of Series 1.

Any further response falls under dissecting the joke territory...
... So here goes.

First, I understand if someone would prefer a broader Benny Hill interpretation, but I'm not the one to write it. Partially because I didn't want to try to recontectualize his humor, and partially because, for chase scenes, I don't think anything I could put in text would be worth including.

And I really just find Yakety Sax amusing.

For me, in addition to the mental images, there's humor in the idea that 1) the Foundation has to deal with this on a regular basis, and 2) that somebody might have caused that. Probably an anartist. I didn't include that because I don't really like anti-Foundation love notes in addenda, and didn't think I could pull one off and still be funny.

Given the pervasive presence of surveillance networks and handheld video recording in first-world nations, any SCP-1955-J affected entities escaping a Foundation facility could result in [DATA EXPUNGED].

It just didn't feel that funny and felt a bit like a speed bump for the flow of the article, but considering that A) This is written well, B) the tone here is good and proper for both an SCP document and the joke you're going for, and C) this is really funny, I have to upvote anyway.
